texts.1.1: INDIAN Methodist Hymn-Book Staylim=Paypa ta Methodist=Ts'hayilth.
texts.1.2: HYMNS used on the Fraser River Indian Mission, of the Methodist Church, B. C. Conference. to which are appended Hymns in Chinook, and the Lord's Prayer and Ten Commandments.
texts.2.1: Rev's. Thos. Crosby, Chas. M Tate, and Wm. H Barraclough, B.A., Missionaries.
texts.2.2: Compiled and Printed by Rev. W.H.Barraclough, Chilliwack, B.C. 1898.
texts.2.4: The following hymns are in the Chill-way-uk dialect of the language of the Alkomaylum nation of Indians, who live along the Fraser River, from Yale to the Coast, and on Vancouver Island, at Cowichan and Nanaimo. The Alkomaylum, (or Ankomeenum, sometimes called Stawlo or River language,) as spoken by the Cowichans, is sweet and rythmical. The Chillwayuk dialect is harsher and more guttural. The Nanaimos, the Yales, the Sumas, the Kwantuls, etc. of B.C., and the Nooksaks of Wash., U.S.A., each speak a slightly different dialect of the same language.
texts.2.6: ` When before k, sound the letter by pressing the back of the tongue against the soft palate, and expelling the letter with a clicking sound. When before t, ts, or tz, press the tip of the tongue against the hard palate, and expel the sound as before.
texts.2.7: kh, Is sounded by lightly pressing the back of the tongue against the soft palate, and emitting the sound in a slurring manner.
texts.2.8: tl, and lth, Are sounded by pressing the tip of the tongue against the hard palate and emit as in kh.
texts.2.9: a, Is pronounced ah; while all others are regular as in English.
texts.2.10: T.C., C.M.T., and W.H.B., at the end of each hymn, are the initials of the translators.

texts.40.4: Nesika Papa, mitlite kopa saghalie, klosh spose konaway tilikum mamook praise Mika nem; klosh spose konaway tilikum mamook tyee mika; klosh spose konaway tilikum kopa okook illahie mamook Mika tumtum, kaw-kwa klaska mamook kopa saghalie-illahie. Okook sun, pe konaway-sun potlatch nesika muk-amuk; pe klosh mika mash okook ma-sa-tchie nesika mamook kopa mika, kaw-kwa nesika mash okook ma-sa-tchie hul-oi-ma tilikum mamook kopa nesika; pe klosh mika mamook help nesika, spose halo-ikta tolo nesika kopa masatchie; pe klosh mika mamook haul nesika spose halo nesika chako kla-how-yum. Klosh spose kawkwa.
texts.40.6: Sawlth Mal, lay kwa tchee-tchilth, ay-e-tcha kwus kwaw-kwa-tchits tomuk mes-tayokh taswas skwikh e-wal ay-e; ay-e-tcha-kwus tomuk mestayokh kwus titheet talowa e-wal See-am; ay-e-tcha-kwus tomuk mestayokh e-tila tumokh, kwus staa-stokh taswas skwilawal staa ta mes-tay-okh lay ta tchee-tchilth tumokh. Awkwus-tawlokh til-alth-le-melth kwus elth-til tila wile; ay-e mela-kul-is-tchuh tasawlth kul-see-ize, staa-tcha-staa mela-kul-is-tchit ta kul-skwi-it-tawlokh ta ow la`tz mes-tay okh; ay-e kwawm-kwum-tchuh tila sawlth skwi-la-wal kwus owa-tchit at ow kwulam ta kul; ay-e-kwus kee-awt'la-mit-taw-lokh kwus owa-tchit tasos-it.
texts.41.1: 1 Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
texts.41.2: 2 Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth; thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.
texts.41.3: 3 Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
texts.41.4: 4 Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labor and do all thy work: but the seventh is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.
texts.41.5: 5 Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
texts.41.9: 9 Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.
texts.41.10: 10 Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbor's.
texts.41.13: 2 Wake mika iskum ikta spose mamook Saghalie-Tyee yaka.
texts.41.14: 3 Wake mika mamook kultus yaka nem Saghalie Tyee.
texts.41.16: 5 Klosh nannitsh mika papa pe mika mamma.
texts.41.18: 7 Wake mika ma-mook ma-sat-chic kona-moxt klootchman.
texts.41.21: 10 Wake mika mamook tumtum spose mika kepswalla huloima tilikum klaska klootchman pe iktas.
texts.41.25: 2 Owa-tchuh ee-ise-okh kwa stem staa kwa T-S.
texts.41.26: 3 Owa-tchuh kal-kul-aylth-okh ta skwikhs kwa Tchee-tchilth-See-am.
texts.41.28: 5 Ay-e-skwas kwaw-kwa-tchit taswa lay mal, ka taswa lay tal.
texts.41.31: 8 Owa-tchuh kwus kal kwa stem tilay kwa latcha.
texts.41.33: 10 Owa-tchuh kwus kwolkwul-aywal kwus sthee-its-tul, ka kwus kal kwus stem.
